author: PavelMakarchuk
body:
The TaxAct OR-40 PDF (page 4) shows tax = **$81,682** — matching PE ($81,680.97 within rounding). So TA and PE agree as you noted; the confusion is about which Chart to use.

Per 2025 OR-40 Instructions, **page 32 (Tax Rate Charts)** verbatim:

> **Chart S** — Single / Married filing separately:
> "If your taxable income is over $125,000 ..... your tax is **$10,627 plus 9.9%** of excess over $125,000"
>
> **Chart J** — Married filing jointly, **Head of Household**, or Qualifying Surviving Spouse:
> "If your taxable income is over **$250,000** ..... your tax is **$21,256 plus 9.9%** of excess over $250,000"

This filer is **HoH** (`mstat=1` + `depx≥1`, the standard TAXSIM convention PE infers as Head of Household) → **Chart J** applies, not Chart S.

Statute-correct calc for HoH at taxable income $860,364:
- $21,256 + 9.9% × ($860,364 − $250,000)
- = $21,256 + 9.9% × $610,364
- = $21,256 + $60,426.04
- = **$81,682.04**

Which matches TaxAct ($81,682) and PE ($81,680.97) within rounding. Your hand calc reading of "$10,627 + 9.9%" was the **Chart S** (Single) thresholds, which is why it didn't match.

TAXSIM-35 returns $83,428.11 — that's the Chart S formula applied to an HoH filer. Could TAXSIM-35 be applying Chart S thresholds for `mstat=1` regardless of dependents? Per the TY 2025 OR-40 instructions, HoH should use the same chart as Joint (Chart J).
